bug_semantics: Starting in 1.3.4, JWSRegistry imposed max_payload_length during deserialization, but the RFC7797 b64=false compact and flattened-JSON branches assigned the unencoded payload without calling validate_payload_size. Oversized lower-trust JWS payloads therefore bypassed the configured bound and could consume excess resources while equivalent b64=true inputs raised ExceededSizeError.
flaw_origin: Commit 05ccff5d3c78e6e84175080ee5c44b713f733e42 introduced JWSRegistry payload-size enforcement and routed the registry into RFC7797 extraction, but placed validate_payload_size only in the b64=true else branches, atomically creating the b64=false enforcement gap.
evidence: The CVE.org CVE-2026-48990 record is PUBLISHED and identifies versions 1.3.4 through 1.6.5 as affected, version 1.6.7 as fixed, and the failure as omitted max_payload_length checks in RFC7797 b64=false compact and flattened JSON deserialization.

Git commit 05ccff5d3c78e6e84175080ee5c44b713f733e42 has the sole parent 7d7733b54bc176c3de5138eaa2bf06a29d234de1 and adds max_payload_length plus validate_payload_size, while its RFC7797 compact.py and json.py hunks call that validator only in b64=true else branches.

Tag 1.3.3 resolves to introducer parent 7d7733b54bc176c3de5138eaa2bf06a29d234de1; 05ccff5d3c78e6e84175080ee5c44b713f733e42 is absent from 1.3.3 and is an ancestor of tag 1.3.4 at 6b6642b7e0f13cb6d8dc4541c1d68ff8523ccf27, matching the first affected release boundary.

At tag 1.6.5, RFC7797 compact extraction assigns payload_segment directly under is_rfc7797_enabled and flattened JSON does the same, whereas both b64=true branches call registry.validate_payload_size(payload_segment).

Direct fix 4d4ea2e787ed36a2190158d86d8470e3acbb349b moves payload validation before the RFC7797 branch in both compact.py and json.py; merge 9186561fc40de112e3b3f01934b11d7ca54da142 incorporates it through PR #97, and the fix is an ancestor of tag 1.6.7 at 1e5b94da589c695f54abd9f1a0ad822dcffe0305.

The introducer's raw commit object and GitHub commit page attribute the single-parent, GPG-signed commit to Hsiaoming Yang <me@lepture.com>; its message is only 'fix(jws): validating content size to avoid DoS' and has no Co-authored-by trailer, AI-tool attribution, generated-by marker, or associated pull request shown. No AI marker exists on the BIC itself.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not the older existence of RFC7797 itself: before 05ccff5d3c78e6e84175080ee5c44b713f733e42 there was no JWSRegistry payload limit to bypass. That commit introduced the limit and applied it asymmetrically, so it is the smallest public atomic introducer; its immediate parent is available and is the 1.3.3 release. The single-parent commit is not a merge or squash aggregate. Commit 4d4ea2e787ed36a2190158d86d8470e3acbb349b directly repairs the advisory's reproduced inline compact and flattened-JSON paths and reaches the declared fixed release. Because the BIC has human attribution and no AI marker in its commit metadata or public commit page, the case is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: The advisory's suggested remediation also mentions detached RFC7797 compact payloads supplied via the payload argument. Commit 4d4ea2e787ed36a2190158d86d8470e3acbb349b did not validate that empty-segment path; commit 683ca24a57c1d2cb25173e7b3eaa49bd68a63aef later added the missing check and first appears in tag 1.7.3. Thus 1.6.7 closes the advisory's demonstrated inline compact and flattened-JSON cases but not that separately described detached variant.
